the_day: Eight US states sued OpenAI over ChatGPT and children, the FTC reportedly subpoenaed OpenAI and Anthropic over safety incidents, Anthropic told investors its quarterly revenue reached $16.8 billion, and Google is moving AI Plus subscribers off Gemini Pro models.

items.headline: FTC subpoenas Anthropic and OpenAI over AI safety incidents
points: The FTC demanded documents from Anthropic and OpenAI about recent safety incidents, Axios first reported, followed by CBS, ABC and The Hill.
Ars Technica says the probe examines whether the companies' security incidents harmed Americans.
Separately, TechRepublic reports EU officials have questioned both companies over AI agent security incidents.

items.headline: Anthropic tells investors quarterly revenue reached $16.8 billion
points: Anthropic told investors its third-quarter revenue rose about 45% to $16.8 billion, according to the FT, WSJ and New York Times.
Several outlets report Anthropic also said it was profitable on an adjusted basis ahead of its planned IPO.
New York City Comptroller Mark Levine urged Anthropic to pause its US IPO over AI safety, Reuters and Bloomberg report.

items.headline: Eight US states sue OpenAI over ChatGPT's effect on children
points: Eight states sued OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms children and young users and deceives parents and adults.
They are Arizona, Arkansas, Idaho, Iowa, Kansas, Montana, Nebraska and West Virginia. Politico calls the coalition bipartisan.
West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey told CNBC the products have been proven unsafe for children.
